# Mixture-of-Experts Transformer Architecture

## Core Architecture

A Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layer replaces standard feed-forward networks (FFNs) in transformer blocks with a set of parallel expert networks and a routing mechanism. The fundamental computation for a token $x$ is:

$$\text{MoE}(x) = \sum_{i \in \text{TopK}(g(x))} g_i(x) \cdot E_i(x)$$

where $E_i$ are expert FFNs, $g_i(x)$ are gating scores from a router network, and TopK selects the $k$ most relevant experts per token.

## Routing Strategies

### 1. Dense (Soft) Routing

All experts are evaluated for every token, and outputs are combined via a softmax-weighted sum:

$$\text{output} = \sum_{i=1}^{N} \text{softmax}(g(x))_i \cdot E_i(x)$$

This computes all $N$ experts per token — **dense computation** with no sparsity benefit. Rarely used at scale.

### 2. Sparse Top-K Routing (Dominant Approach)

Only the top-$k$ experts (typically $k=2$) are activated per token:

$$\text{output} = \sum_{i \in \text{TopK}(g(x), k)} g_i(x) \cdot E_i
